title: Plugins: camera, filesystem, notifications, geolocation and preferences

videos.script:
A page in a browser cannot keep a reminder for tomorrow morning. It cannot take a photo with the camera's own app, or keep data the system promises not to clear. A phone app can. {{phone}}

Capacitor's plugins are how the planner asks. {{plugins}} Each one is an npm package with three implementations of the same call. One in Java or Kotlin, one in Swift, and one for the web. {{three}} Your code calls one function, and Capacitor picks the right side.

Today the planner gets five of them. {{five}} It keeps the plan, so a reload no longer loses it. It writes a file. It reminds you on the morning of a session. It says where you are. And it takes a photo of your notes.

Each one asks permission the way a phone does. {{ask}} And each one needs a line or two in the native projects, or the phone refuses. {{native}} You will run all of it in the browser, and you will see exactly where the browser stops standing in for a phone.
